rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.6 and 3.1-3.4 report the authors' own model runs (monthly soil water balance IR = ETc - EP using WorldClim data over 39,316 km2 of Colombian Hass avocado production zones), validation against 73 weather stations (Figure 3), water deficit maps (Figure 5, Table 2) and an ANN relevance analysis of ITCZ influence (Figure 6).
rows.notes: The study does not report any result on precise water use during phenological stages, reduced irrigation applications, or water savings. It only computes and maps the regional monthly irrigation requirement (water deficit) of Hass avocado, finding that 99.8% of the potential production area needs irrigation at least one month a year. The IR model is a simplified monthly soil water balance (Penman-Monteith ETo x Kc minus effective precipitation), not an energy balance model of a field, and no irrigation scheduling was applied or tested; the maps are only proposed as a future scheduling tool. This is at most a precondition (identifying when/where irrigation is required) of the claimed water-conservation effect. Validation was of ETo code and WorldClim data against weather station IR, not of any water-saving outcome. Phenological stages are not analysed.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.6 and 3.1-3.4 report the authors' own regional model runs of monthly irrigation requirement for Hass avocado in Colombia, validated against weather station data (Figure 3), with water deficit maps (Figure 5, Table 2) and an ANN analysis of ITCZ influence (Figure 6).
rows.notes: The study reports no yield or productivity data of its own. The only productivity statements (yield increase under drip irrigation at Kc = 0.75; water deficit reducing yield and fruit quality) are cited from Grajales [23] and other literature in the Introduction and Discussion, which do not count. The study only maps where and when irrigation is required; it does not test any scheduling model's effect on maintaining productivity. At most it supports a precondition (need for irrigation) of the claimed effect.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references), with some OCR duplication of lines from two-column/overlapping page layouts but no missing sections. The study is a regional GIS water-balance mapping exercise (irrigation requirement from WorldClim climate data), not a field trial of a scheduling tool or energy balance model; it reports no irrigation applications, water savings, or yield outcomes of its own.
